title: Container Bookings: Amount of Roll Compensation and the Per-Booking Ceiling
content:
This page defines the amount of Container Bookings roll compensation credited for a qualifying carrier roll, including how the per-booking ceiling limits it.

## Rule

The provisional credit is the product's per-container roll compensation multiplied by the containers compensated. Where the product's rate stands at 0.00, the provisional credit is nil; nothing is credited and the charge history receives no compensation entry.

The room left under the ceiling is the product's per-booking compensation ceiling less the amounts of the roll compensation entries already credited on the booking, and it is never taken below zero. The amount credited is the smaller of the provisional credit and that remaining room. Rounding to two decimal places happens only on this final amount.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Assume an invented per-container compensation of 212.00, 6 containers compensated, an invented ceiling of 3000.00 and 2400.00 already credited on the booking.

- Provisional credit: 212.00 multiplied by 6, which is 1272.00.
- Room left under the ceiling: 3000.00 less 2400.00, which is 600.00.
- Amount credited: the smaller figure, 600.00.

Had nothing been credited earlier, the room would be 3000.00 and the full 1272.00 would be credited. Had 3000.00 already been credited, the room would be 0.00 and nothing could be added. None of these figures is a product value.
